images.title: A ship can defend its water
images.caption: The ivory rival vessel marks its occupied hex with a dashed outline and shield. Its hex cannot be entered. The straight destination beyond it is outside the remaining two-hex budget; this fixture does not claim every longer route is cut off.

images.title: World view keeps a way back
images.caption: Return is visible beside Home and Fleet. A physical touch on the rival ship’s hex leaves Sail disabled and does not snap to a nearby legal destination or change the camera.

images.title: Capture starts as a proposal
images.caption: The selected vessel is previewed in your colour while Alexander remains the listed owner. Native assertions verify ownership and position remain unchanged until Capture is confirmed; restarting before confirmation discards the proposal.

images.title: Confirmed capture opens the route
images.caption: After Capture is confirmed, the former blocker belongs to you. The two-hex route through that friendly vessel is now legal. This image shows a sailing proposal; the Sail button still commits the voyage.

images.title: The completed voyage survives restart
images.caption: After confirming Sail and terminating the app, Resume retains both ships’ positions, captured ownership and the charted map. The proposal disappears and the ordinary turn controls return.

images.title: A blocked launch explains why
images.caption: All launch cells on this player’s owned coast are occupied by rival vessels. Ship is unavailable despite sufficient wood, ore and wool, and the reason names the opposing ships. Tapping it spends no cards.

images.title: The full instruction stays visible
images.caption: At Accessibility XXXL, “Sail your ship” and the full two-line blockade explanation are visible. The compact maritime instruction is capped visually at Large; Fleet and the rulebook retain unrestricted larger-text inspection.

images.title: An ordinary match reaches a winner
images.caption: An earlier native scripted match reached the actual end-game screen: Tokugawa won at 14 VP and Alex finished with 7 VP. This image belongs to the first focused run, before the later instruction-readability correction.

images.title: Retained failure: truncated instructions
images.caption: The earlier largest-text screen drew an ellipsis in the sailing title and explanation even though accessibility-label assertions passed. This failed visual result motivated the scoped text correction and rendered-pixel OCR check. It is not the corrected current screen.

images.title: Ordinary Release build, ready to start
images.caption: A fresh simulator install of the Release app launched with no QA arguments and survived six seconds without a new app crash report. Rules, New Game and Leaderboard are legible. This is simulator runtime evidence; physical iPhone installation and play were not observed.
images.captureTimeSource: Original PNG filesystem modification timestamp; runtime and review receipts retain their independent verification times.

limitations: Corrected screenshots are seven selected native checkpoints, not exhaustive manual scrutiny of every game state.
The ordinary winner image predates the dock readability correction; its first-run source inputs are identified separately.
The raw attachment manifests retain the complete source inventory, including captures not selected for this portable gallery.
Audit authorship is disclosed in each raw receipt; the readability reviewer authored the initial QA/test files.
The 48 functional games and six separate-process repeats establish functionality and determinism, not comparative AI strength.
Gate and delivery status is historical at the export timestamp; later delivery requires root-owned final receipts.

The original status-at-export.json remains the earlier historical pending snapshot. status-latest.json and final gate receipts supersede its gate status only; release and device delivery remain pending.
